No new file/router/middleware modified or replaced any pre-existing Traefik config.

No new service publishes a host port; port 80/443 is claimed only by the pre-existing coolify-proxy, per docs/ARCHITECTURE.md.

realBugsFoundAndFixedThisPass.bug: Signup email-verification bypass in the frontend
realBugsFoundAndFixedThisPass.detail: apps/web/src/lib/auth.ts's signUp() saved GoTrue's /signup response as a real Session unconditionally. With ENABLE_EMAIL_AUTOCONFIRM=false (the real configured value), an unconfirmed signup response has no access_token — the saved 'session' had access_token: undefined, and Signup.tsx always navigated to /app/upload regardless, rendering the UI as if logged in. This is exactly the kind of email-verification bypass this project must never claim as 'signup works', even though every subsequent authenticated API call would have failed with a real 401.
realBugsFoundAndFixedThisPass.fix: signUp() now returns a discriminated result; the frontend shows a real 'Check your email' state and does not navigate in unless a genuine access_token was returned.
realBugsFoundAndFixedThisPass.foundVia: code read while wiring the real signup flow, not a test failure

realBugsFoundAndFixedThisPass.bug: Missing JWT_SECRET in the new hasheemstudio-api container
realBugsFoundAndFixedThisPass.detail: Every authenticated route (e.g. POST /v1/uploads/sessions) returned a real 500 'Missing required env var JWT_SECRET' because the new container's environment: block omitted it.
realBugsFoundAndFixedThisPass.fix: Added JWT_SECRET: ${JWT_SECRET} to the api service in infra/compose/docker-compose.yml.
realBugsFoundAndFixedThisPass.foundVia: a real Playwright browser run against the live public domain, not a code review — see diag-upload run in session log

realBugsFoundAndFixedThisPass.bug: CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS leaking production origins into local bare-host dev
realBugsFoundAndFixedThisPass.detail: Initially set via the shared /etc/hasheemstudio/local.env file, which a bare-host `pnpm dev` apps/api process also reads directly (apps/api/src/env.ts) — this would have silently broken local dev's CORS allowlist (blocking http://127.0.0.1:5173).
realBugsFoundAndFixedThisPass.fix: Hardcoded the production origins directly in the api service's compose environment block instead of interpolating the shared env var; removed CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS from local.env entirely so bare-host dev falls back to its own code default.
realBugsFoundAndFixedThisPass.foundVia: self-review before commit, not a test failure

incidentDisclosure.what: While removing a stale CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS line from /etc/hasheemstudio/local.env via `sed -i` (a Bash command, not the normal secret-safe helper scripts), the session harness's automatic 'file changed on disk' notification printed the full contents of the changed lines, which included the real values of RESEND_API_KEY and CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN, into the conversation transcript.
incidentDisclosure.recommendation: Rotate both RESEND_API_KEY and CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN out of an abundance of caution, then re-provision the new values through the same Vaultwarden flow used earlier this session.
incidentDisclosure.mitigationGoingForward: Avoid raw `sed`/shell edits to /etc/hasheemstudio/local.env; route changes through the existing helper scripts (fetch-vaultwarden-secret.sh and the wire-smtp/set-public-urls pattern used this session), which read and write values without ever printing them.
